# Learning Section Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add a dedicated Learn section to the NUST Prep Electron app — topic browser with section tabs, full lesson view (concept + rules + examples + mistakes + tips + mini quiz), accessible from home and mid-test.

**Architecture:** Three JSON files (`data/learning/verbal_lessons.json`, etc.) generated by Claude Code routine, each containing all topics for that section as lesson objects. Two new page states (`"learn"`, `"lesson"`) added to the existing vanilla-JS single-file app. All UI reuses existing CSS classes from `index.html`.

**Tech Stack:** Electron 28, vanilla JS, no framework, no test runner — verification via manual smoke tests in the running app.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add `load-lessons` IPC handler to `main.js`**

```js
ipcMain.handle("load-lessons", (_, section) => {
  const filePath = path.join(LEARNING_DIR, `${section}_lessons.json`);
  if (fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
    return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8"));
  }

});

}

## Task 5: `renderLearn()` — topic browser

**Files:**
- Modify: `app/index.html`

- [ ] **Step 1: Add `topicAccuracy` and `lessonReadTime` helper functions**

In `index.html`, find the `// ── Learn actions ──` block added in Task 4. Insert these helpers just before it:

```js
// ── Learn helpers ──
function topicAccuracy(section) {
  const m = {};
  sessionsFor(section).forEach(s => (s.details || []).forEach(d => {
    if (!m[d.topic]) m[d.topic] = { c: 0, t: 0 };
    m[d.topic].t++;
    if (d.correct) m[d.topic].c++;
  }));
  return m; // { "Topic Name": { c: 3, t: 5 } }
}

function lessonReadTime(lesson) {
  const text = [
    lesson.summary || "",
    ...(lesson.key_rules || []),
    ...(lesson.worked_examples || []).map(e => `${e.question} ${e.wrong} ${e.correct} ${e.why}`),
    ...(lesson.common_mistakes || []),
    ...(lesson.exam_tips || []),
  ].join(" ");
  return Math.max(1, Math.round(text.split(/\s+/).length / 200));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Replace `renderLearn()` stub with full implementation**

Find the stub `function renderLearn(app, notifHTML) { ... }` added in Task 3 and replace it entirely with:

```js
function renderLearn(app, notifHTML) {
  const sec = state.learnSection;
  const s = SECTIONS[sec];
  const acc = topicAccuracy(sec);
  const wk = weakTopics(sec);
  const lessons = state.lessons;

  // Sort: weak topics first, then alphabetical
  const sorted = [...lessons].sort((a, b) => {
    const aWeak = wk.includes(a.topic);
    const bWeak = wk.includes(b.topic);
    if (aWeak && !bWeak) return -1;
    if (!aWeak && bWeak) return 1;
    return a.topic.localeCompare(b.topic);
  });

  // Filter by search query
  const query = (state.learnSearch || "").toLowerCase().trim();
  const filtered = query ? sorted.filter(l => l.topic.toLowerCase().includes(query)) : sorted;

  const weakCount = sorted.filter(l => wk.includes(l.topic)).length;
  const totalCount = sorted.length;

  const tabBtn = (key) => {
    const ts = SECTIONS[key];
    const active = key === sec;
    return `<button class="btn ${active ? '' : 'btn-ghost'}" style="${active ? 'background:' + ts.color : ''};flex:1" onclick="switchLearnSection('${key}')">${ts.icon} ${ts.label}</button>`;
  };

  const topicCards = filtered.map((lesson, i) => {
    const isWeak = wk.includes(lesson.topic);
    const topicAcc = acc[lesson.topic];
    const pct = topicAcc ? Math.round(topicAcc.c / topicAcc.t * 100) : null;
    const readTime = lessonReadTime(lesson);
    const borderStyle = isWeak
      ? 'border-color:rgba(239,68,68,0.4);background:rgba(239,68,68,0.06)'
      : '';
    const accBadge = pct !== null
      ? `<span class="tag" style="background:${pct < 60 ? 'rgba(239,68,68,0.15)' : pct < 75 ? 'rgba(245,158,11,0.15)' : 'rgba(16,185,129,0.15)'};color:${pct < 60 ? '#fca5a5' : pct < 75 ? '#fcd34d' : '#6ee7b7'}">${pct}%</span>`
      : `<span style="color:var(--text-muted);font-size:11px">not studied</span>`;

    // Find actual index in state.lessons (not sorted index)
    const realIndex = lessons.indexOf(lesson);

    return `<div class="card" style="cursor:pointer;${borderStyle}" onclick="openLesson(${realIndex})">
      <div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center">
        <div>
          <div style="font-size:14px;font-weight:600;color:${isWeak ? '#fca5a5' : 'var(--text)'}">
            ${lesson.topic}
            ${isWeak ? `<span class="tag" style="background:rgba(239,68,68,0.15);color:#fca5a5;margin-left:6px">WEAK</span>` : ''}
          </div>
          <div style="font-size:11px;color:var(--text-muted);margin-top:3px">~${readTime} min read</div>
        </div>
        <div style="text-align:right">${accBadge}</div>
      </div>
    </div>`;
  }).join("");

  const emptyState = totalCount === 0
    ? `<div class="card" style="text-align:center;padding:32px;color:var(--text-muted)">
        No lessons yet.<br><br>
        <span style="font-size:12px">Tell Claude Code: <span style="color:var(--blue-light);font-style:italic">"Generate learning content for NUST Prep"</span></span>
       </div>`
    : filtered.length === 0
    ? `<div class="card" style="text-align:center;padding:24px;color:var(--text-muted)">No topics match "<span style="color:var(--text)">${state.learnSearch}</span>"</div>`
    : topicCards;

  app.innerHTML = `${notifHTML}
  <div class="header">
    <div class="container">
      <div>
        <h1 style="font-size:22px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-0.02em">Learn</h1>
        <p style="color:var(--text-dim);font-size:12px;margin-top:4px">${totalCount} topics${weakCount ? ` · <span style="color:#fca5a5">${weakCount} weak</span>` : ''}</p>
      </div>
      <button class="btn btn-ghost" onclick="state.page=state.lessonPrevPage;render()">← Back</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="container no-drag" style="padding-top:20px">
    <div class="btn-row" style="margin-bottom:12px">
      ${tabBtn("verbal")}${tabBtn("analytical")}${tabBtn("quantitative")}
    </div>
    <input
      type="text"
      placeholder="Search topics…"
      value="${state.learnSearch.replace(/"/g, '&quot;')}"
      oninput="state.learnSearch=this.value;render()"
      style="width:100%;background:rgba(255,255,255,0.03);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;color:var(--text);font-size:13px;font-family:inherit;outline:none;margin-bottom:12px"
      class="no-drag"
    />
    ${weakCount > 0 && !query ? `
    <div class="card" style="background:rgba(239,68,68,0.06);border-color:rgba(239,68,68,0.25);margin-bottom:4px">
      <div style="font-size:12px;color:#fca5a5;font-weight:600">⚠ Weak topics — prioritize these</div>
      <div style="font-size:11px;color:rgba(255,255,255,0.4);margin-top:4px">${wk.join(' · ')}</div>
    </div>` : ''}
    ${emptyState}
  </div>`;
}
```

## Task 6: `renderLesson()` — full lesson view + interactive quiz

**Files:**
- Modify: `app/index.html`

- [ ] **Step 1: Replace `renderLesson()` stub with full implementation**

Find the stub `function renderLesson(app, notifHTML) { ... }` added in Task 3 and replace it entirely with:

```js
function renderLesson(app, notifHTML) {
  const lesson = state.currentLesson;
  if (!lesson) { state.page = "learn"; render(); return; }

  const sec = lesson.section || state.learnSection;
  const s = SECTIONS[sec] || { accent: "#60a5fa", color: "#2563eb" };
  const acc = topicAccuracy(sec);
  const topicAcc = acc[lesson.topic];
  const pct = topicAcc ? Math.round(topicAcc.c / topicAcc.t * 100) : null;
  const isWeak = pct !== null && pct < 60;

  const rulesHTML = (lesson.key_rules || []).map(rule =>
    `<div style="border-left:3px solid var(--green);padding:8px 12px;background:rgba(5,150,105,0.06);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;font-size:13px;color:var(--text-dim);margin-bottom:6px">${rule}</div>`
  ).join("");

  const examplesHTML = (lesson.worked_examples || []).map(ex => `
    <div class="card" style="padding:14px 16px;margin-bottom:8px">
      ${ex.question ? `<div style="font-size:12px;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:8px">${ex.question}</div>` : ''}
      <div style="font-size:13px;color:#fca5a5;margin-bottom:4px;text-decoration:line-through">✗ ${ex.wrong}</div>
      <div style="font-size:13px;color:#6ee7b7;margin-bottom:6px">✓ ${ex.correct}</div>
      <div class="explanation">${ex.why}</div>
    </div>`
  ).join("");

  const mistakesHTML = (lesson.common_mistakes || []).map(m =>
    `<span class="tag" style="background:rgba(239,68,68,0.12);color:#fca5a5;margin:3px 4px 3px 0;display:inline-block">${m}</span>`
  ).join("");

  const tipsHTML = (lesson.exam_tips || []).map(t =>
    `<div style="font-size:13px;color:#fcd34d;padding:6px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.04)">💡 ${t}</div>`
  ).join("");

  const quizHTML = (lesson.quiz || []).map((q, qi) => {
    const chosen = state.lessonAnswers[qi];
    const answered = chosen !== undefined;
    return `<div class="card" style="margin-bottom:10px">
      <div style="font-size:14px;color:#f1f5f9;margin-bottom:12px;line-height:1.6">
        <span style="color:var(--text-muted);font-weight:700;margin-right:8px">${qi + 1}.</span>${q.question}
      </div>
      ${["A","B","C","D"].map(opt => {
        if (!q.options[opt]) return '';
        const isCorrect = opt === q.correct;
        const isChosen = opt === chosen;
        let cls = "";
        let letterStyle = "background:rgba(255,255,255,0.08)";
        if (answered) {
          if (isCorrect) { cls = "correct"; letterStyle = "background:var(--green)"; }
          else if (isChosen) { cls = "wrong"; letterStyle = "background:var(--red)"; }
        } else if (isChosen) {
          cls = "selected"; letterStyle = "background:var(--blue)";
        }
        return `<button class="option-btn ${cls}" onclick="${answered ? '' : `state.lessonAnswers[${qi}]='${opt}';render()`}" style="${answered ? 'cursor:default' : ''}">
          <span class="option-letter" style="${letterStyle}">${answered ? (isCorrect ? '✓' : (isChosen ? '✗' : opt)) : opt}</span>
          <span style="padding-top:4px;line-height:1.5">${q.options[opt]}</span>
        </button>`;
      }).join("")}
      ${answered && q.explanation ? `<div class="explanation">💡 ${q.explanation}</div>` : ''}
    </div>`;
  }).join("");

  app.innerHTML = `${notifHTML}
  <div class="header">
    <div class="container" style="align-items:center">
      <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;flex:1;min-width:0">
        <button class="btn btn-ghost" style="flex-shrink:0" onclick="state.page='learn';render()">←</button>
        <div style="min-width:0">
          <h1 style="font-size:18px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-0.02em;color:${s.accent};white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis">${lesson.topic}</h1>
          <p style="color:var(--text-dim);font-size:12px;margin-top:2px">${SECTIONS[sec].label}${isWeak ? ' · <span style="color:#fca5a5">⚠ weak — focus here</span>' : ''}</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="container no-drag" style="padding-top:20px">

    ${lesson.summary ? `
    <div class="card">
      <div style="font-size:11px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:8px">Concept</div>
      <div class="explanation" style="font-size:14px;line-height:1.7">${lesson.summary}</div>
    </div>` : ''}

    ${rulesHTML ? `
    <div class="card">
      <div style="font-size:11px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:10px">Key Rules</div>
      ${rulesHTML}
    </div>` : ''}

    ${examplesHTML ? `
    <div class="card">
      <div style="font-size:11px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:10px">Worked Examples</div>
      ${examplesHTML}
    </div>` : ''}

    ${mistakesHTML ? `
    <div class="card">
      <div style="font-size:11px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:8px">Common Mistakes</div>
      ${mistakesHTML}
    </div>` : ''}

    ${tipsHTML ? `
    <div class="card">
      <div style="font-size:11px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--text-muted);margin-bottom:8px">Exam Tips</div>
      ${tipsHTML}
    </div>` : ''}

    ${lesson.quiz && lesson.quiz.length > 0 ? `
    <div style="font-size:13px;color:var(--text-dim);font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;margin:20px 0 10px">Mini Quiz · ${lesson.quiz.length} questions</div>
    ${quizHTML}` : ''}

    <div style="height:32px"></div>
  </div>`;
}
```

## Task 7: Wire up `init()` + live-reload listener

**Files:**
- Modify: `app/index.html`

- [ ] **Step 1: Load lessons on startup in `init()`**

Find the `async function init()` block (around line 592):

```js
async function init() {
  await loadData();
  render();

  // Listen for new question files from Claude Code
  if (window.nustPrep && window.nustPrep.onQuestionsUpdated) {
    window.nustPrep.onQuestionsUpdated(async (filename) => {
      state.availableDays = await window.nustPrep.listAvailableDays();
      notify(`New questions ready: ${filename}`);
    });
  }
}
```

Replace with:

```js
async function init() {
  await loadData();
  state.lessons = await window.nustPrep.loadLessons(state.learnSection);
  render();

  if (window.nustPrep && window.nustPrep.onQuestionsUpdated) {
    window.nustPrep.onQuestionsUpdated(async (filename) => {
      state.availableDays = await window.nustPrep.listAvailableDays();
      notify(`New questions ready: ${filename}`);
    });
  }

  if (window.nustPrep && window.nustPrep.onLearningUpdated) {
    window.nustPrep.onLearningUpdated(async (filename) => {
      state.lessons = await window.nustPrep.loadLessons(state.learnSection);
      if (state.page === "learn") render();
      notify(`Learning content updated: ${filename}`);
    });
  }
}
```

## Task 8: Update `CLAUDE.md` — learning generation routine

**Files:**
- Modify: `CLAUDE.md`

- [ ] **Step 1: Add learning generation step to CLAUDE.md**

Open `CLAUDE.md`. After the existing `## Step 7: Sync to App Data Directory` section, add a new section:

```markdown
## Step 8: Generate Learning Content (First Run Only)

Check if all 3 lesson files exist:
- `/Users/Shared/nust-prep/data/learning/verbal_lessons.json`
- `/Users/Shared/nust-prep/data/learning/analytical_lessons.json`
- `/Users/Shared/nust-prep/data/learning/quantitative_lessons.json`

If **any** file is missing, generate **all 3** files.

Each file is a JSON array of lesson objects — one per topic. Topics are fixed (see below). Generate content independently of `progress.json` — do not weight topics by accuracy. Every topic gets equal depth.

### Topics per section

**Verbal (11 topics):** Subject-Verb Agreement, Parallelism & Sentence Structure, Modifier Placement, Tense Consistency, Sentence Correction, Reading Comprehension, Synonyms & Antonyms, Vocabulary in Context, Analogies, Sentence Completion, Critical Reading

**Analytical (12 topics):** Syllogisms, Conditional Logic (If-Then), Strengthen & Weaken Arguments, Assumption Questions, Paradox & Explain, Data Interpretation, Linear Arrangement, Circular Arrangement, Blood Relations, Direction Sense, Coding-Decoding, Ranking & Ordering

**Quantitative (13 topics):** Percentages, Ratio & Proportion, Profit Loss & Discount, Time Speed & Distance, Work & Pipes, Number Properties & Divisibility, Probability & Combinatorics, Geometry & Mensuration, Coordinate Geometry, Sequences Series & Interest, Quadratic Equations, Averages & Mixtures, Algebra & Inequalities

### Lesson object schema

Each topic must produce one object matching this exact schema:

```json
{
  "topic": "Exact topic name from list above",
  "section": "verbal|analytical|quantitative",
  "summary": "2-3 sentence concept explanation — clear, exam-focused",
  "key_rules": ["Rule 1", "Rule 2", "Rule 3"],
  "worked_examples": [
    {
      "question": "Problem or sentence scenario",
      "wrong": "Incorrect version or answer",
      "correct": "Correct version or answer",
      "why": "1-sentence explanation of why"
    }
  ],
  "common_mistakes": ["Mistake 1", "Mistake 2", "Mistake 3"],
  "exam_tips": ["Tip 1", "Tip 2"],
  "quiz": [
    {
      "question": "Question text",
      "options": { "A": "...", "B": "...", "C": "...", "D": "..." },
      "correct": "B",
      "explanation": "Why B is correct"
    }
  ]
}
```

Requirements:
- `key_rules`: 3–5 rules
- `worked_examples`: 2–3 examples
- `common_mistakes`: 2–4 items
- `exam_tips`: 2–3 tips
- `quiz`: exactly 3–5 MCQs with verified correct answers
- All math quiz answers must be arithmetically verified

Save files to `/Users/Shared/nust-prep/data/learning/` then run:

```bash
git -C /Users/Shared/nust-prep add data/learning/
git -C /Users/Shared/nust-prep commit -m "Generate learning content for all sections"
git -C /Users/Shared/nust-prep push origin main
git -C /Users/Shared/nust-prep pull origin main
```

If all 3 files already exist, skip this step entirely.

To **regenerate** (explicit refresh): user will say "regenerate learning content" — overwrite all 3 files and commit as above.
```

```bash

git commit -m "docs: add learning content generation step to CLAUDE.md routine"
```

```bash
cat > /Users/Shared/nust-prep/data/learning/verbal_lessons.json << 'EOF'
[
  {
    "topic": "Subject-Verb Agreement",
    "section": "verbal",
    "summary": "Subjects and verbs must agree in number and person. A singular subject requires a singular verb; a plural subject requires a plural verb. The key challenge is identifying the true subject when intervening phrases are present.",
    "key_rules": [
      "Singular subjects take singular verbs: 'The dog runs'",
      "Plural subjects take plural verbs: 'The dogs run'",
      "Intervening phrases between subject and verb do not affect agreement",
      "Collective nouns (team, committee) take singular verbs in standard usage"
    ],
    "worked_examples": [
      {
        "question": "Identify the error:",
        "wrong": "The quality of the reports were poor.",
        "correct": "The quality of the reports was poor.",
        "why": "Subject is 'quality' (singular), not 'reports'. 'of the reports' is an intervening phrase."
      },
      {
        "question": "Choose the correct form:",
        "wrong": "Neither the manager nor the employees was present.",
        "correct": "Neither the manager nor the employees were present.",
        "why": "With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the closer subject: 'employees' (plural)."
      }
    ],
    "common_mistakes": [
      "Agreeing with the nearest noun instead of the true subject",
      "Treating collective nouns as plural",
      "Errors with neither/nor and either/or constructions"
    ],
    "exam_tips": [
      "Cross out prepositional phrases to isolate the true subject",
      "For neither/nor and either/or, verb agrees with the subject closest to it"
    ],
    "quiz": [
      {
        "question": "Choose the correct sentence:",
        "options": {
          "A": "The group of students are working hard.",
          "B": "The group of students is working hard.",
          "C": "The groups of student are working hard.",
          "D": "The group of students were working hard."
        },
        "correct": "B",
        "explanation": "'Group' is the singular subject; 'of students' is an intervening phrase. Singular subject → singular verb 'is'."
      },
      {
        "question": "Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?",
        "options": {
          "A": "Neither the teacher nor the students was ready.",
          "B": "Neither the teacher nor the students were ready.",
          "C": "Neither the teachers nor the student were ready.",
          "D": "Neither the teacher nor the student are ready."
        },
        "correct": "B",
        "explanation": "With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the closer subject: 'students' (plural) → 'were'."
      },
      {
        "question": "Select the correctly constructed sentence:",
        "options": {
          "A": "Each of the candidates have submitted their forms.",
          "B": "Each of the candidates has submitted their forms.",
          "C": "Each of the candidate have submitted their form.",
          "D": "Each of the candidates have submitted his forms."
        },
        "correct": "B",
        "explanation": "'Each' is always singular regardless of the prepositional phrase that follows. 'Each...has' is correct."
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "topic": "Parallelism & Sentence Structure",
    "section": "verbal",
    "summary": "Parallelism requires that grammatically equal ideas be expressed in the same grammatical form. When items appear in a list or comparison, they must all use the same part of speech and structure.",
    "key_rules": [
      "Items in a list must use the same grammatical form",
      "Comparisons must use matching structures",
      "Correlative conjunctions (both/and, either/or, not only/but also) require parallel elements"
    ],
    "worked_examples": [
      {
        "question": "Fix the parallelism error:",
        "wrong": "She enjoys reading, writing, and to swim.",
        "correct": "She enjoys reading, writing, and swimming.",
        "why": "'to swim' is an infinitive; it must be a gerund like the other items: 'swimming'."
      }
    ],
    "common_mistakes": [
      "Mixing infinitives (to run) with gerunds (running) in the same list",
      "Inconsistent tense in parallel clauses"
    ],
    "exam_tips": [
      "Scan sentences for lists and comparisons first — they are the most common parallelism test site",
      "Identify the first item's form, then verify all other items match"
    ],
    "quiz": [
      {
        "question": "Which sentence is correctly parallel?",
        "options": {
          "A": "He likes to run, swimming, and cycling.",
          "B": "He likes running, to swim, and cycling.",
          "C": "He likes running, swimming, and cycling.",
          "D": "He likes to run, to swim, and cycles."
        },
        "correct": "C",
        "explanation": "Option C uses all gerunds (-ing forms): running, swimming, cycling. All items are grammatically identical."
      },
      {
        "question": "Identify the parallel error:",
        "options": {
          "A": "The report was thorough, accurate, and well-written.",
          "B": "The report was thorough, accurate, and written well.",
          "C": "The report was thorough, accurately done, and well-written.",
          "D": "The report was thorough, accurate, and concise."
        },
        "correct": "C",
        "explanation": "'Thorough' and 'well-written' are adjectives; 'accurately done' is an adverb+verb phrase. It breaks the adjective pattern."
      }
    ]
  }
]
EOF
```
